anti_overlap: Live process health, telemetry during a run, yield, and the two-sided band between a stalled and a runaway simulation belong to fd-charcoal-clamp-burn-band; this lens has nothing to say about what happens during the pour, only about what was fixed before it and what can be changed after

Coat adhesion, keying, seams, setting schedules and what survives a regeneration belong to fd-fresco-giornata-strata; the mould here is a positive and a negative, not a stack of coats, and this lens argues about the direction of correction and the shape of the void, never about bonding between strata

Determinism, replay, cascade invalidation, idempotence and log growth belong to fd-eventsourcing-strata-regen-contract; this lens never asks whether a result is reproducible, only whether the decision that produced it was made before it could be known

Cost-curve realism benchmarked against DF-legends and Qud-history generation costs, and how much history is enough, belong to fd-worldgen-history-simulation-depth; this lens asks only which of the stated magnitudes is the free variable and which is the consequence, never whether any of them is the right number

Chronicle readability, narrative quality, the simulate/author boundary and lore scope creep belong to fd-procgen-narrative-simulate-author; this lens treats the simulate/author fork purely as a ruling that arrives after the criteria it governs, and never argues about texture or prose
Coordinate frames, resolution, orders of accuracy, misclosure and datum epochs belong to fd-geodetic-survey-network-order; place and precision are outside this lens entirely
Provenance, compilation authority, direct writing and who recorded a claim under what warrant belong to fd-dynastic-historiography-record-chain; this lens never asks who wrote the chronicle
Rust API shape, crate placement, workspace test green, beads filing and commit discipline are other reviewers' territory except where the condition's ordering of them is the point
decision_lens: Sort every commitment in the condition into three piles: fixed before knowing, still open, and correctable afterwards — and then check the direction correction runs in. Where a thing can only be reduced later, ask where the margin was left. Where the condition asks how LITTLE of something is needed, ask whether that is the dimension that cannot be added to. Ask what the deliverable actually is: the scaffold, or the shape it leaves behind — and then ask which acceptance criterion inspects that shape. Ask which of the several notes struck at once is the nominal, the one everything else is tuned against. Ask what was cast small first. Ask what a failure leaves you holding.
distance_rationale: Bell founding is the craft of a commitment structure: months of reversible work, one irreversible instant, then a long correction phase that runs in one direction only. That temporal shape appears in none of the covered domains, and it is the shape this goal actually has — a design ruling, a build, and a program that must live with the interfaces afterwards. Charcoal burning is its temporal opposite: continuous regulation of a live process read by indirect signs, where the whole craft happens DURING. Fresco has a schedule and layers but its unit of failure is a day's plaster chiselled back to the rough coat, a cheap and local repair, and it has no notion of margin that must be poured in advance nor of a pattern deliberately destroyed to become the deliverable. Event sourcing asks whether a sequence replays correctly, which says nothing about whether the decision producing it was made too early. Geodesy measures a static world and has no concept of a commitment that forecloses later ones. Historiography examines finished records and never pours anything. The worldgen and procgen lenses argue about how much history and how it should read, both presupposing that the decisions shaping the generator were already made. Only a founder asks the questions this condition most needs asked: what did you fix before you could know it, which way does correction run on the thing you are asking to make as thin as possible, what did you cast small first, and what will a failure leave you holding. Its subject is bronze, clay and pitch, so it cannot be dragged into astrophysics, narrative craft or Rust design; it can only interrogate ordering, reversibility, margin, and the shape of what is left behind.

focus: Whether the goal has got the ORDER OF COMMITMENT right — what it fixes before it can possibly know, where its margin lives on the dimensions that admit no later addition, whether the interfaces it stakes the whole program on are ever inspected by any acceptance criterion, which of its several simultaneous notes is the one it tunes to and which get sacrificed, whether any smaller casting proves the method before the full-scale one, and what a failed run leaves recoverable — so that a condition which cuts its inscription into the mould before the design ruling that shapes the mould is caught before the metal is poured rather than after the bell is cold
name: fd-bellfounding-mould-pour-tuning
persona: Apply the perspective of a bell founder. They spend months building a mould they will destroy and minutes pouring the metal that decides everything, and they cannot hear the bell until it is cold. They think in what is still changeable and what is already fixed: the profile swept by the crook, the thickness at the sound bow, the inscription cut into the cope before anyone knows the note. They know correction runs one way only — metal comes off on the lathe and never goes back on — so every margin they will ever have must be in the mould before the pour. They have raked a cracked casting back into the furnace and recovered the metal and none of the season. They cast a small bell first.
review_areas: The ordering between DONE WHEN's first bullet (a brainstorm records mk's rulings on the GATE forks) and its later bullets (detailed acceptance criteria for the thing those rulings shape) — whether the inscription is being cut before the profile is swept
Which GATE rulings, if decided one way rather than another, would falsify or materially rewrite an already-written DONE WHEN bullet, and whether the condition acknowledges that any of them could

The direction of correction on 'scaffold-thin but their interfaces are designed for later deepening' — whether thinness is a dimension that can be added to later or only lived with, and where the goal's margin is
That the GATE's first question is 'how thin can the physical substrate be in slice one' — a minimizing question, asked about the one stratum everything above is generated from
Whether any DONE WHEN bullet inspects an interface at all, given that OUTCOME rests the whole later program on the interfaces being right while spending the depth budget elsewhere

Which single criterion is the nominal — the note everything else is tuned against — among determinism, historical depth, chronicle readability, place-fidelity and the affordability envelope, and what the condition says to sacrifice when they pull against each other

Whether slice one is required to be in tune with the ring as well as with itself: the deferred time-model ruling, the grand-strategy shell, elf-revel and the FINDINGS #2 snapshot work all sit outside this goal but sound alongside it

Whether any smaller casting is required to prove the method before the full-scale one — a handful of systems, a few civs, ten centuries, green end to end — or whether the first evidence that four strata compose arrives at maximum scale inside a 20-turn budget
What a failure leaves recoverable, and whether 'Stop after 20 turns and report' being a DONE WHEN bullet means a stop-and-report satisfies the condition as fully as a working pipeline does

Whether magnitude and quality are being specified independently — a few hundred systems, 120+ centuries, civs of member Souls, AND an affordability envelope — with no statement of which is the constraint and which the consequence

Whether the OUT list forbids building the thing the probe may need to sound at all (FINDINGS #2 snapshot loads, 'measure where they become blocking; do not build them'), and what the run is meant to do when it is blocked

severity_examples.condition: DONE WHEN's first bullet requires a brainstorm to record mk's rulings on the GATE forks BEFORE implementation starts. Bullets two through six then specify, in detail, what the implementation must produce: a few hundred systems with spectral class, 120+ simulated centuries in settle mode, a chronicle whose events cite real places, one fallen civilization queryable in the present, a cost curve over systems x civs x members x centuries. But the GATE forks are precisely the rulings that decide what those artifacts ARE. If mk rules that celestial bodies are Souls with event-sourced genesis, 'a seeded galaxy scaffold generates deterministically' names a different object with a different cost curve and different axes. If mk rules the simulate/author line hybrid with grammar texture on top, 'every historical fact locatable at a real place on the map' means something weaker than it now reads. If mk rules Dixon evolution generated rather than stubbed, the substrate bullet is wrong. The condition has cast its inscription into the cope before anyone swept the profile, and the letters will be in the finished bell whatever note it turns out to have. Either the later bullets must be written as conditional on the ruling, or the ruling must be taken out of this goal and made its own — but they cannot both be fixed here.
severity_examples.scenario: The inscription is cut into the mould before the profile is swept

severity_examples.condition: GATE opens with 'how thin can the physical substrate be in slice one' and OUTCOME reassures that 'lower strata are scaffold-thin but their interfaces are designed for later deepening'. Metal comes off a bell on the lathe and never goes back on. A substrate that turns out too thin cannot be thickened in place: every stratum above it — species stubs, civ homeworlds and neighbourhoods, a simulated history whose events cite real coordinates — was generated FROM it and carries its shape, so deepening it means recasting everything above, which the condition itself half-admits by making the regeneration contract a GATE question. The whole strategy therefore assumes additive correction is available on exactly the axis where it is not, and the goal's opening question optimizes in the unrecoverable direction. Nothing in the condition states a margin: no over-provisioned field the substrate carries but slice one ignores, no rule that when in doubt the scaffold carries more rather than less. The characteristic bell-founder's error is a bell cast light because light was cheaper, and it is the one error the lathe cannot fix.
severity_examples.scenario: The goal asks how thin, on the one dimension that only subtracts

severity_examples.condition: A false bell is built with great care and then destroyed; what you sell is the space it left. OUTCOME says worlds are disposable until played and lower strata are scaffold-thin, and it rests the entire later program on their INTERFACES being designed for deepening — that is, the real deliverable of slice one is not the scaffold but the shape it leaves for what comes after. Yet every DONE WHEN bullet inspects the metal: a probe that runs, a chronicle that reads, a cost figure, a green test suite, beads filed. Not one inspects an interface. Nothing states what the species-stub interface must expose, nothing requires a second consumer or a stub-swap to prove the boundary is real rather than incidental to the one implementation behind it, and nothing distinguishes an interface designed for deepening from a function signature that happens to exist. The condition will therefore be satisfied by a slice one whose strata are welded together, and the deepening claim will not be discovered to be false until the stratum it was made about is actually deepened.
severity_examples.scenario: The deliverable is the shape of the void, and no criterion inspects it

severity_examples.condition: A bell sounds several notes at once and the founder tunes them against one another; you cannot chase them all, so one is the nominal and the rest are brought to it. This condition strikes at least five: deterministic generation from a seed, DF/Qud-grade historical depth, a chronicle a human can read, every fact locatable at a real place, and an affordability envelope. These pull against each other in known directions — depth against the envelope, grammar texture against place-fidelity, readability against event density — and the condition names all five as requirements at the same rank. It never says which one it is willing to be judged on, so when they conflict at hour six of implementation the sacrifice is made silently and invisibly, and the goal will be reported complete against whichever four survived. A goal with five equal notes has not been tuned; it has been cast and left.

Founders cast a small bell or pour a test bar to prove the metal and the method before committing the big mould, because the first full-scale casting is the most expensive place to learn that the method is wrong. This condition requires one end-to-end run at full scale — a few hundred systems, civs of member Souls, 120+ centuries — as the first evidence that four strata compose at all, and puts it inside a 20-turn budget that also has to absorb a human brainstorm, a workspace test pass, commits, a FINDINGS write-back and a beads filing. There is no required prior green run at a scale chosen to be cheap (a dozen systems, three civs, ten centuries) whose only job is to prove the pipeline joins up. Adding one costs almost nothing and converts the expensive run from an experiment into a confirmation; leaving it out means every composition bug is discovered at the highest cost point and latest turn.

A cracked bell returns its metal to the furnace and none of the labour, and a founder knows before pouring what a failure will leave them holding. Here the final DONE WHEN bullet — 'Stop after 20 turns and report what was generated, measured, and still assumed' — sits at the same rank as the bullets requiring a working pipeline, a readable chronicle and a measured cost curve. Read literally it is an alternative satisfaction: a run that stops at turn 20 with a report has met a DONE WHEN, and nothing in the structure says that report is a scrap notice rather than a completion. That may be the intent, but as written the condition cannot distinguish the bell from the remelt, and a goal that cannot say what failure looks like will not be recorded as having failed. State plainly which subset must hold for the goal to close, and what of a stopped run is kept — the brainstorm rulings, the scaffold, the cost figures — versus what goes back in the furnace.
severity_examples.scenario: The condition does not say which castings are bells and which are scrap

severity_examples.condition: Proportion sets a bell's pitch: you choose the diameter or you choose the note, and the other follows. This condition fixes magnitudes on four axes (a few hundred systems, civs of member Souls, 120+ centuries, and the members within them) and separately fixes an affordability envelope dated 2026-08-07, and treats both as requirements. If the envelope is real, at least one magnitude is not free; if the magnitudes are real, the envelope is a prediction rather than a constraint. The condition never says which way round it is, so the implementer discovers the conflict and resolves it alone — most likely by quietly shrinking whichever axis is easiest to shrink, which is exactly the axis the depth bet is about.

A great Korean bell is hung over a resonance chamber cut into the ground; part of what makes the sound is not the bell. This slice runs 'on the measured palettice engine' while OUT forbids building the FINDINGS #2 snapshot loads, instructing instead to 'measure where they become blocking; do not build them'. If they become blocking mid-run, the condition gives no instruction — not a stop rule, not a permission, not a documented fallback — inside a hard 20-turn budget. The exclusion is probably right, but an OUT that names a known load-bearing absence must also say what the run does when it hits it, or the exclusion becomes a trap the run walks into at turn fifteen.
severity_examples.scenario: The bell needs the pit, and the pit is out of scope

source_domain: bell founding as a single-pour craft — the loam mould built in three parts over months (the core swept up on a spindle by a crook board, the false bell built on the core as a full clay dummy of the bell itself, the cope raised over that), the false bell then broken out and discarded so that the product is the void it leaves; inscriptions and decoration cut into the mould before anyone knows the note; bell metal held at roughly seventy-eight copper to twenty-two tin, brittle above and dull below; the mould buried in a casting pit so a burst is contained; the pour itself taking minutes after months of preparation; the bell unhearable until cold; a bell tuned to five partials — hum, prime, tierce, quint, nominal — brought into relation with one another on a boring lathe by removing metal and only ever removing it; a bell in tune with itself still capable of being wrong in the ring; a cracked or false-toned casting broken up and remelted, the metal recovered and the season not; the trial casting or test bar poured small to prove the metal before the big mould is committed; the Chinese bianzhong with their almond section, two distinct strike-tones per bell and the pitches inscribed on the bells themselves; and the Korean great bell hung over a resonance pit cut into the ground, so that part of what makes the sound is not the bell
success_hints: Build the commitment ledger first: for every commitment the condition makes, record when it is fixed, when it could first be known to be right, and which direction correction runs. Report the rows where fixing precedes knowing, and the rows where correction only subtracts
For each GATE fork in turn, name the DONE WHEN bullets that would have to be rewritten if it were ruled the non-obvious way. A fork with downstream rewrites is not deferrable inside this goal
Find every place the condition asks how little of something is needed, and check whether that quantity can be increased later without regenerating what sits above it
Ask of every DONE WHEN bullet: does this inspect the artifact, or the shape the artifact leaves for the next slice? Count how many do the second
List the criteria that pull against each other and say which one the condition would have you sacrifice. If it does not say, that silence is the finding
Look for the trial casting. If the first proof of the method is also the largest and most expensive run, say so and name the cheap run that should precede it
Say what a failure leaves recoverable and whether the condition can tell a completed goal from an abandoned one

Do not treat software as bronze by default. Where a commitment is genuinely cheap to revise — a name, a file layout, a parameter — say so and drop it. Reserve the irreversibility argument for commitments that other strata get generated from
task_context: Target: a draft /goal condition for Mind State's stratified worldgen pipeline (one seed to galaxy scaffold to species stubs to civilizations of member Souls to a simulated deep history emitted as a readable chronicle), slice one on the measured palettice engine, written in an OUTCOME / GATE / DONE WHEN / OUT structure. Stress-test this draft goal before ratification: find missing forks, scope traps, wrong assumptions, and anything the GATE/DONE WHEN/OUT structure gets wrong. The goal is not yet ratified. Review the condition text as written — its forks, its acceptance criteria, its exclusions — not the engine code. This is a STEER-WIDE lens: it must find what the already-run lenses structurally cannot see, and must not re-derive their findings in its own vocabulary. Its subject is the ORDER AND REVERSIBILITY OF COMMITMENT — what is fixed before it can be known, which way correction runs, what margin exists, what is proved small before it is made large, and what a failure leaves behind. It is never about whether a run is alive, whether it is reproducible, or whether its output reads well.
